clue.text: Note I'd stress without a line

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the stress word wraps round the I'd

parts.note: stress means accent, emphasis on a syllable
I'd taken as the letters of the contraction

explanation.surface: A music student is told to play a note, putting the stress on it, without any line of the stave.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a sharp, flat or natural sign outside the key signature is called an accidental, a kind of note marking.

clue.text: What's with the DJ? Flip side tackle, I gather

parts.note: the flip side of a record is its B-side, giving the letter B

indicators.note: to gather things is to pull them together into a new heap, so the letters of tackle and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a disc jockey is doing, guessing he is tackling the other side of a record.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ looks like a disc jockey, but here it is the British abbreviation for dinner jacket, the formal suit that goes with a dress code.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner jacket is worn at events whose dress code is named after the dark bow tie that goes with it.

clue.text: Condemn not the daughter! No! I rise as protector of her unborn child

indicators.note: not the daughter means the word for condemn loses its D

parts.note: to condemn is to damn
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the letters are read upwards, so No and I are turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An anguished plea not to condemn a pregnant daughter, made by someone who stands up to protect her baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns NO I into ION; the clue's exclamations are part of the drama but the No and I are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The amnion is the membrane forming the fluid-filled sac that surrounds and shields a developing foetus in the womb.

explanation.definitionFit: The Bedlington is a terrier breed from Northumberland, known for its lamb-like woolly coat.

clue.text: Lehar composition, one of five for him, "On With The Motley!"

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of the composer's name are arranged anew

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

explanation.surface: A piece by the operetta composer Lehar, one of five he wrote, set to the words of a famous aria.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay makes HARLEQUIN, the motley-clad pantomime character; under the preamble the grid takes his partner, his sweetheart COLUMBINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a famous tenor aria line about putting on a clown's costume, and a motley chequered costume is the trademark of the pantomime lover.

a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A warning that water left flowing will rust a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into metal, as acid or rust does, is to wear it away, which is what corroding means.

clue.text: What makes Burgundy religious? No! Not frenzied Irish!

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so religious

indicators.note: frenzied describes things thrown out of order, so the two exclamation words swap places

explanation.surface: A puzzled drinker asks what makes a wine region devout, and is answered with a protest against wild Irishmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What makes Burgundy' is the definition: not a colour, but the grape behind the wine. 'frenzied' throws the first word to the end, so NONOT becomes NOTNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Burgundy wine is made almost entirely from this black grape variety.

clue.text: Shelled helping its loveless opposite, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement of the letters that follow
love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so loveless means losing an O

explanation.surface: A serving set out across the table from someone, with no love lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops an O from opposite, giving PPOSITE; with ITS that is rearranged, as 'perhaps' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Small young peas are served out of their pods, so a dish of them is a portion of something shelled.

clue.text: Bearing canisters to explode first underground

indicators.note: letters that explode fly apart and land in a new order

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Containers of explosive carried by the wartime underground, set to go off first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' says the bearing E joins the fodder before the explosion; the answer is the wartime underground movement.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground is a secret movement fighting an occupying power, as in wartime France.

clue.text: Car's way to get into accident

indicators.note: get into says the way-to piece is placed inside the word for accident

parts.note: a hap is a chance happening, an accident
RD, road, is a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver's route that ends up in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car's' is the definition with 's as is; 'accident' looks like part of the scene but is the outer word, HAP, an old word for chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a motor car with a rigid roof, as opposed to a soft-top convertible.

an overly flattering write-up or plug in the press

explanation.walkthrough: The double definition gives PUFF; under the preamble the grid takes its partner from the phrase about huffing and puffing.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag on a cigarette and a gushing promotional notice share the same short word.

explanation.definitionFit: A pianola is a self-playing piano operated by a perforated roll, so it plays the noted roll.

definitions.text: One element in conflict with another

parts.words: One element in conflict with another
parts.note: one of the four classical elements, the one that puts out the other, fire

explanation.definitionFit: Of the ancient four elements, the wet one quenches the hot one, so they are natural enemies.

explanation.surface: A breakfast at a Freemasons' lodge where no smoked herring is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kipper' looks like the smoked fish beside masonic cookery, but it is a sleeper, from kip, a nap.
